newsitem.title: USA: Shell sees no threat to Nautilus from ANR Pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Shell sees no threat to Nautilus from ANR Pipeline.

text.p: U.S. regulators should approve construction of competing natural gas pipelines in the Gulf of Mexico and let the market decide whether they are all needed or not, Shell Gas Pipeline Co president Doug Krenz said Thursday.
Shell is one of three owners of a proposed $220 million pipeline, the Nautilus project, awaiting approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
On Wednesday, Coastal Corp's ANR Pipeline Co asked the FERC to hold a hearing to compare the Nautilus project with a competing Gulf of Mexico pipeline proposal by ANR.
ANR said Nautilus would be unnecessary if its own pipeline was built, and that its pipeline would cost less and require fewer new facilities with less harm to the environment.
Krenz said he was aware of the request, but added that the Nautilus project could stand on its own.
"We feel our project is well-supported by market demand," he said. "There is a lot of gas coming on in that area."
Shell and its partners Marathon Oil Co and Leviathan Gas Pipeline Partners LP have secured commitments from shippers to use the 600 million cubic feet per day of capacity to be built.
Marathon and Shell have major deepwater acreage in the Green Canyon area to be served by the planned pipelines.

"The theme that we tried to go by in this arena is what the FERC is using as its policy these days -- let the market determine what is the best solution with respect to various pipeline alternatives," he said.
ANR is seeking to add 461 million cubic feet per day of capacity to the 1.1 billion cubic feet per day of offshore Louisiana production it now delivers.
